messages.author: e498b38f01df2491
messages.subject: besag model - bad PIT histograms
parts:
Dear group,

I am fitting a 'besag' model to the response variable 'number of calves of humpback whales' using a binomial distribution.

As I have a set of covariates, I fitted 4 models and compared them through DIC and PIT histograms (visual analysis and KS test). Nevertheless, the PIT histograms are really different from a uniform distribution (even when I recalculated CPO and failure = 0).

Even though, the predicted occurrence probabilities from these models are totally reasonable in terms of humpback whale ecology.

I have already tried a Poisson error distribution to the response 'number of calves of humpback whales' and the PIT showed the same pattern.

My dataset have a length of 123, where 56 observations are 0, 10 observations are 1,1 observation is 3 and 1 observation is 4. The rest is completed with NA (where I intend to predict occurrence).

The PIT histograms are available here: https://www.dropbox.com/sh/bydyihyl2lzl1a4/AAA9lX_yRLk7N3bf8koOKexma?dl=0

My questions are:
Can I present the results even with these PIT histograms?
Should I change anything in the model to improve PIT?

Thank you in advance for your help.

Best regards,
Heloise

On Tue, 2016-02-16 at 13:02 -0200, Heloíse Pavanato wrote:
> Dear group,
>
> I am fitting a 'besag' model to the response variable 'number of
> calves of humpback whales' using a binomial distribution.
>
> As I have a set of covariates, I fitted 4 models and compared them
> through DIC and PIT histograms (visual analysis and KS test).
> Nevertheless, the PIT histograms are really different from a uniform
> distribution (even when I recalculated CPO and failure = 0).
>
> Even though, the predicted occurrence probabilities from these models
> are totally reasonable in terms of humpback whale ecology.
>
> I have already tried a Poisson error distribution to the response
> 'number of calves of humpback whales' and the PIT showed the same
> pattern.
>
> My dataset have a length of 123, where 56 observations are 0, 10
> observations are 1,1 observation is 3 and 1 observation is 4. The
> rest is completed with NA (where I intend to predict occurrence).

the pit-histogram will be different in this case, as the response is
discrete, not continous. so with poisson data, then it would not be
uniform, even for the true model (check yourself, sampling data from
mean = exp(1), and then compute the pit hisotram. )

only for continous response, you'll get uniform. 

there is a paper discussing this, I think, Leo Held, Czado, and
someeone, cannot recall all details.

H

messages.author: b82c68dca2181495
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] besag model - bad PIT histograms
parts:
Heloise,

All analysis I performed considering a Poisson likelihood gave me PIT histograms exactly like yours.

As Prof. Harvard said, discrete distributions will probably not yield uniform distributed PIT values as continuous (ex. Gaussian) variables will.

I think the paper he is referring to is this one:
Czado, ., Gneiting, T. and Held, L. (2009). Predictive model assessment for count data, Biometrics.

This presentation may help you too.
http://www.informatik.uni-ulm.de/ni/staff/HKestler/Reisensburg2009/talks/held.pdf

Best Regards,
Bruno
